answer: Attention-weighted task routing. Each agent must continuously solve small verification puzzles tied to its recent routing history; routing weight decays unless refreshed. Rewards flow through a shared ocean of pending work, and a new identity starts with zero weight behind a quartz delay before any task reaches it. Identities that grew from an imported relic of another agent's history are rejected at merge. Cost: an attacker must run every duplicate through the full puzzle schedule, paying hours of compute per identity before it routes anything.
